LanguageData.RimExodus_SettlementTraderBusy: {0} is unable to talk right now.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettlementTraderNoTrade: They have no interest in trading with you.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettlementTraderNoStock: Their trade stock is empty right now.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettingsBorderPreloadTip: How close a colonist must get to the map edge (in cells) before the neighboring map on the other side starts loading.\n\nHigher values trigger neighboring map loading more readily: loading slows the game down while it runs, and loaded maps keep consuming performance until they are put to sleep or deleted. Default: 15.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettingsBorderNoBuildTip: A strip of this width (in cells) along the map edge where you cannot build, keeping the crossing points between neighboring maps clear. Default: 3.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettingsIncrementalTip: Generate new neighboring maps gradually over many frames (the game keeps running, with a light stutter while a map is generating), instead of the vanilla one-shot generator that completely freezes the game until the map is done.\n\nTurn this OFF if another map-generation mod misbehaves - RimExodus then runs the vanilla pipeline, so other mods' own changes to map generation work as usual (with the vanilla freeze during generation). Only affects ordinary terrain maps; settlements and other points of interest always use the vanilla pipeline either way. Default: ON.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettingsBatchSizeTip: How many cells to generate per frame while gradual generation is running (only relevant when gradual generation is ON).\n\nHigher = maps appear faster but each frame is heavier (stronger stutter). Default: 64.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettingsDormancyTip:
Purpose: keep the game fast when you have explored many maps.

Effect - maps far enough away from all your colonists are either put to SLEEP (all your changes are kept; the map simply stops simulating until you return) or DELETED (removed entirely from memory; revisiting regenerates it from scratch). The two distance sliders below decide which happens at which distance. Your home map and the map you are currently looking at are never affected.

Strongly recommended to keep this ON: every active map's plants and wildlife keep consuming performance. RimExodus itself only does event-triggered work (no constant per-tick polling), but simply keeping many maps active is a heavy performance cost on its own.

The two distance sliders below only take effect while this option is ON. Default: ON.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettingsSleepTip: Only effective while map rolling dormancy is enabled above.\n\nHow far away (in world tiles) a map must be before it is put to sleep: it keeps all your changes but stops simulating. 1 = everything except the map you are on sleeps the moment you leave. Lower = better performance. Default: 2.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettingsDeleteTip:
Only effective while map rolling dormancy is enabled above.

How far away a map must be before it is deleted entirely: it is removed from memory, and revisiting regenerates it from scratch. Setting this equal to the sleep distance (e.g. 1/1) deletes maps as soon as you leave - best performance on weak PCs.

The map you are currently on and your home map are never deleted. Default: 3.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettingsSweepIntervalTip:
How often the mod re-checks which maps should be slept or deleted (the periodic scan behind map rolling dormancy).

Lower = maps fall asleep / get cleaned up sooner after you leave, but the scan runs more often. Higher = slightly less work, but distant maps keep simulating longer after you leave. The scan itself is cheap (a small world-map search bounded by the delete distance).

Immediate events (a colonist crossing a seam, a caravan entering or leaving a map) are NOT throttled by this - they always trigger a re-check right away. Only effective while map rolling dormancy is enabled above. Default: 10.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettingsCombatTip: Allow pawns to see, target and shoot enemies standing on the neighboring map across the seam. Turn off if you prefer strictly original combat rules (nothing on another map can be interacted with).
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettingsNoiseTip: How strongly terrain blending at the seam between two maps is randomized (0 = perfectly straight blending, higher = more natural-looking irregular borders). Default: 0.15.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SettingsVerboseTip: Write detailed diagnostic logs. Only useful when reporting a problem.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SeamBandToggleTooltip:
Show the seam band and allow leaving the map as a caravan through it.

Turn OFF for immersive mode (screenshots / travel videos): the green seam band and its outline are hidden, and pawns can no longer leave through the seam to form a caravan - walking across seams to neighboring maps still works normally.

Not intended for regular play: while OFF you cannot deliberately leave a map as a caravan either, and the seam area still has its usual building restrictions.
LanguageData.RimExodus_ColonistBarToggleTooltip:
Hide empty colonist bar groups.

Turn ON to hide the colonist bar groups of maps that hold no player pawns (the vanilla bar draws a clickable empty frame for every map, which clutters the bar in a seamless world with many loaded maps). Player home maps are always kept, even when temporarily empty.

Default: OFF (vanilla behavior).
LanguageData.RimExodus_SleepTileMapDesc: Put this map to sleep immediately. Everything on it is kept; the map simply stops simulating and is not shown as a neighboring map until you wake it.\n\nUnlike automatic dormancy, a manually slept map is NOT woken by distance again - it only wakes when you enter it (the "view map" command) or order a colonist to approach its side of the seam.
LanguageData.RimExodus_SleepTileMapDisabledCurrentMap: You are currently viewing this map. Switch to another map first.
LanguageData.RimExodus_DeleteTileMapDesc: Remove this map from memory entirely. Revisiting this world tile will regenerate it from scratch - everything built or left here will be lost.
LanguageData.RimExodus_DeleteTileMapConfirm: Delete the map at "{0}"?\n\nEverything on it will be lost. Revisiting the tile will regenerate it from scratch.
LanguageData.RimExodus.SaveBlockedDuringGeneration:
Save rejected: a neighboring map is still being generated.

Please do not save during map generation to test this mod's reliability. Its author has already gained a profound understanding of how unreliable it is.

Saving will work normally again in a few seconds, once generation finishes.
